title: Reading or Guessing? Visual Grounding Failures of Vision-Language Models for OCR in Ancient Greek Editions
abstract: arXiv:2605.27750v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Recent work has shown that Vision-Language Models (VLMs) used for optical character recognition (OCR) can generate plausible but visually unsupported text, suggesting reliance on language priors. Comparing open-weight VLMs with traditional OCR baselines on low-resource Ancient Greek critical editions, we show that VLM errors often remain fluent even when wrong, producing plausible Greek substitutions where traditional engines produce local recognition noise. To analyze visual evidence during decoding, we introduce controlled image perturbations and token-level grounding measures based on conditional versus image-free decoding distributions. translated_title: 阅读还是猜测？视觉语言模型在古希腊语版本OCR中的视觉定位失败
translated_abstract: 近期研究表明，用于光学字符识别（OCR）的视觉语言模型（VLM）可能生成看似合理但缺乏视觉支持的文本，这表明其依赖语言先验。通过在低资源古希腊语校勘本上将开放权重的视觉语言模型与传统OCR基线进行比较，我们发现视觉语言模型的错误即使出错时也往往保持流畅，产生看似合理的希腊语替换词汇，而传统引擎则产生局部识别噪声。为了分析解码过程中的视觉证据，我们引入了受控图像扰动以及基于条件解码分布与无图像解码分布对比的token级定位度量。在字符级扰动下，视觉语言模型与被扰动的真实文本严重偏离，而传统OCR则相对保持忠实；然而，token级分析表明，对先验的依赖是模型特定的：在一个OCR专用模型中，流畅的词汇错误产生时几乎没有……
tldr: 该论文通过受控图像扰动和token级定位分析，揭示了视觉语言模型在低资源古希腊语OCR任务中依赖语言先验而非视觉证据，导致错误仍然流畅合理，而传统OCR引擎的错误则更忠实于视觉内容，且这种先验依赖程度因模型而异。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals through controlled image perturbations and token-level grounding analysis that Vision-Language Models rely on language priors rather than visual evidence in low-resource Ancient Greek OCR, producing fluent yet unsupported errors where traditional OCR remains visually faithful, with prior reliance varying across models.
